messages:
arjun: quick heads-up — noticed a 12% bump in TTFT for /v1/chat on region-us-east-1 starting ~08:13 UTC after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. latency heatmap attached to the probe but raws look like kernel_time now accounts for ~78% of token latency (used to be ~55%).

maya: ugh. saw spikes too. any change in kv cache hitrate around that time? could be prefetching gone bad or extra evictions.

arjun: kv hitrate dropped ~6% for that route. sample traces show more KVCACHE_MISS per token on long contexts (>1024). interestingly decode queue wait hasn't grown much. so TTFT shift = kernel compute, not scheduling.

kevin: can we get per-token kernel attribution in traces? i.e., split token latency into kernel_cpu, kernel_wait, kv_fetch, decode_loop. current probe aggregates are too coarse.

maya: agreed. proposal: add micro-histograms tagged by route/model/variant for kernel_op (matmul/softmax/kv_lookup) + kv_hit boolean. also emit per-token sampled traces every Nth token to limit overhead.

zara: also tag with batch_size and seq_len buckets. ops needs that to correlate with target-route SLOs. dashboard should expose p50/p95/p99 for each tag.

perf-bot: automated-probe: run=kernel_attrib_sample_v2 started at 08:20 UTC, sample_rate=1/500 tokens, duration=10m. preflight passed. link: https://redwood.internal/perf/probes/17824

luis: volunteering to wire dashboards — can someone drop an example query for the telemetry store? curious how you want kernel_time split recorded.

kevin: use this proto for exporter (pseudocode):
```
metric: token_latency_sample {
  route: string
  model_version: string
  token_idx: int
  seq_len: int
  batch_size: int
  kernel_ops: { name: string, micros: int }[]
  kv_hit: bool
  ttft_micros: int
}
```
Query idea: sum by kernel_ops.name and kv_hit to produce stacked bars per-route.

maya: can we do a canary rollout of the new selector with kernel-attrib on only 5% of traffic? want to compare identical load but with attribution enabled vs baseline. if overhead is <2% we can sweep.

arjun: yes — let's add a feature-flag route param and a rollout config. set sample_rate lower on canary to be safe.

luis: dashboard plan: 1) token-attrib waterfall per-route (p50/p95 kernels stacked) 2) kv-hit vs ttft scatter per seq_len bucket 3) rollout diff widget (canary vs baseline). will start workbook.

zara: add alert if kernel_time_p95 increases >15% over 1h for any customer route. also alert on kv_hit drop >5% over 30m.

perf-bot: probe results (08:20-08:30): sampled 18k tokens, avg overhead 0.8% (CI 0.5-1.2%), kernel_time share observed 80% on canary vs 56% baseline. full report: https://redwood.internal/perf/reports/17824

arjun: thanks. next steps: (1) implement kernel-op micro-histograms + kv_hit flag (maya/kevin) (2) perf probe sweep with canary flag (perf-bot/luis) (3) dashboard + alerts (luis/zara) (4) re-evaluate after 90m of canary traffic. assigning tasks in JIRA.

kevin: one more — add a small synthetic probe for long contexts to stress kv-prefetch path (seq_len 2048, batch=1) so we can isolate prefetch overhead vs kernel perf.

maya: noted. will add to the probe plan. :thumbsup:

arjun: awesome — ping me when dashboards are live and probe link updated. thanks everyone.
